title: Coral and the Will
premise: True-crime podcaster Odile Kavanagh built his quiet life in Saltmere around the unsolved 1998 disappearance of schoolteacher Coral Vance, keeping the town's secrets organized like evidence. When twin letters arrive — one confessing to Coral's murder, one promising 'the rest is buried where the will was read' — Odile realizes the writer knows details never made public, details only he and the original investigators possessed. As he reopens the case on-air, the confessor begins killing again to erase witnesses, and Odile discovers the letters are a trap designed by Coral's daughter, now grown, who believes Odile himself helped bury the truth. In the flooded cellar beneath the old Kavanagh house, Odile confronts the real killer — his own late father's business partner, the executor of Coral's will — and chooses to broadcast the confession live, trading his town's belonging for the truth, and finding a new family in the people who stay anyway.
about_author: Vesper Okonkwo is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing cold-case evidence in coastal county courthouses before turning to fiction. Their work explores how small towns remember, and what they agree to forget.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Twelve years after Coral Vance vanished, Odile records the final episode of his dormant podcast, walking listeners through his immaculate case files. A neighbor's kindness at the diner shows the found-family warmth of Saltmere — and how carefully he keeps everyone at arm's length. Beat: comfortable loneliness about to crack.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Two letters arrive in the same envelope: one confesses to Coral's murder, the other promises 'the rest is buried where the will was read.' The confessor cites a detail — the color of Coral's scarf — that was never in any public record. Beat: dread and exhilaration; the cold case breathes again.

chapters.title: The Will Was Read
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with a flashback to 1998. Odile digs out probate records and learns Coral's will named an executor: Ambrose Pell, his late father's business partner and the closest thing Odile had to an uncle. Beat: betrayal's first cold touch.

chapters.title: Episode One: Coral
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Against his own instincts, Odile releases the letters on-air. The town reacts — some grateful, some hostile; Coral's childhood friend Maren slams a note against his door: 'Stop digging. Some of us buried children with her.' Beat: the cost of truth begins accruing.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Photographs
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren remembers Coral's daughter, Wren, who left town at nine and was never told the truth. She mails Wren a copy of Odile's episode. Beat: grief and guilt; a fuse is lit that Odile can't see.

chapters.title: Second Letter, First Body
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A second letter arrives naming 'the first witness' — and that night, retired deputy Hollis Grady, who took the 1998 missing-persons call, drowns in shallow water. Beat: the confessor is real, and killing.

chapters.title: Sheriff's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dana Okoye's POV. Dana inherited the cold case and her father's shame at botching it. She warns Odile off but shares one sealed detail to test him — and realizes he knows more about the file than she does. Uneasy alliance forms. Beat: wary partnership.

chapters.title: Ambrose Pell, Executor
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile visits the dying, oxygen-tanked Ambrose, who denies everything with terrifying calm and says: 'Your father read that will, boy. Ask what he was paid to skip.' Beat: the past reaches into Odile's own name.

chapters.title: What Father Knew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, interleaved with 1998 flashback. Odile finds his father's ledger: a payment from Pell the week Coral vanished, and a note — 'cellar stays dry, stay out of it.' Beat: Odile's identity as neutral archivist collapses.

chapters.title: The Listener
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, unnamed to the reader. A stranger arrives in Saltmere, checking into the inn, listening to every episode, photographing the courthouse. She befriends Maren under a false name. Beat: the trap closes from a direction Odile never expects.

chapters.title: Episode Seven Goes Wrong
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Mid-broadcast, someone calls in playing a recording of Coral's voice — from the day she disappeared. Odile freezes on-air; the town hears him lose his composure. Dana traces the call to a payphone that shouldn't exist. Beat: humiliation and terror; the killer is toying with him.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren admits to Odile that she saw Coral's car at the Kavanagh house the night she vanished and stayed silent — for Odile's father's sake. 'I chose your family over her. Don't you dare make me regret it twice.' Beat: found family fractures under old debt.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The third letter is addressed to 'the archivist' and contains a page torn from Odile's own case file — the copy only he owns. The confessor has been inside his house. Beat: violation; nowhere is safe.

chapters.title: Wet Cellar, Dry Records
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana searches the sealed Kavanagh cellar and finds it flooded, exactly as the 1998 report described — too neatly. She pulls the original flood-inspection records and finds Pell's signature on a falsified permit. Beat: the machinery of the cover-up surfaces.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Inn
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, still unnamed. The stranger saves Maren from a staged 'accident' on the inn stairs, then vanishes. Maren realizes the woman's eyes are Coral's. Beat: revelation for the reader, dread for the town.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, named at last. Wren reveals herself to Odile: she wrote the letters. The confession was bait to drag him — the son of the man who helped — into exposing the truth he'd been 'filing' for twelve years instead of solving. Beat: fury, grief, and the terrible fairness of her accusation.

chapters.title: Where the Will Was Read
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Reconstructing the phrase, Odile realizes Coral's will was read in the Kavanagh parlor — above the cellar. His father didn't skip a page; he hid one. Odile descends into the flooded cellar at low tide. Beat: descent, literal and moral.

chapters.title: The Executor's Hand
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax part one. In the cellar, Odile finds Coral's remains and the hidden will page naming Pell as sole beneficiary of her estate — motive. Pell appears, alive and far stronger than his oxygen tank suggested, and confesses with the serenity of a man tidying files. Beat: the killer unmasked.

chapters.title: Live Broadcast
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax part two. Trapped, Odile triggers his live-streaming rig — broadcasting Pell's confession to the town. Pell attacks; Wren and Dana arrive; Maren's testimony seals the case. Odile chooses the truth over protecting his father's name and his own belonging. Beat: sacrifice and survival.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Pell is arrested; the town reels. Some doors close to Odile forever. Dana reopens every cold case his father touched. Beat: the cost made real, and the beginning of repair.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren scatters her mother's ashes and, instead of leaving, stays — moving into Coral's old cottage. She and Odile, bound by damage rather than blood, begin the slow work of family. Beat: belonging redefined.

chapters.title: Episode Twenty-Two: Coral and the Will
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The final episode: Odile reads Coral's hidden will aloud, names every person who stayed silent — including himself — and signs off by handing the archive to Wren and the town. The last line: 'Some cases aren't solved. They're carried, together.' Beat: catharsis, accountability, and open-hearted ending.
